cards.explanation: The answer is to contend earnestly for the faith. Jude says he felt it necessary to “…urge you to contend earnestly for the faith entrusted once for all to the saints.” Notice the word earnestly, friends. That's not a casual "I'll get to it after my nap," that's both hands in the dough.

The answer is that it was handed over complete. Jude says the faith was “…entrusted once for all to the saints.” Once for all means it was handed over one time, not delivered in installments, friends. It's like my stamp: it comes down one time, and the lines are already carved in.

The answer is a license for immorality. Jude says these men “…turn the grace of our God into a license for immorality…” They take something generous and treat it like a permission slip. That's like finding the cookie jar open and deciding it means the whole bakery is free for the taking.
The answer is True. Jude says these men “…deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.” They crept in among the believers, friends, and they still deny Him. That's why Jude felt he had to write.

The answer is False. Jude says Jesus delivered His people out of the land of Egypt, and afterward “…He destroyed those who did not believe.” It's a sober reminder, friends, and Jude says they were already fully aware of it. Unbelief had consequences even for people who'd been rescued.

The answer is in eternal chains under darkness. Jude says of those angels, “…these He has kept in eternal chains under darkness, bound for judgment on that great day.” They left their proper dwelling, and now they're held until that day. It's a heavy line, friends, so I'll just let it sit.

The word is example. Jude says Sodom and Gomorrah “…are on display as an example of those who sustain the punishment of eternal fire.” They're held up like a warning sign by the road, friends. Jude puts them on display on purpose.

The answer is "The Lord rebuke you." Michael, the archangel, says, “The Lord rebuke you!” Jude says he “…did not presume to bring a slanderous charge…” against the devil. Even in that dispute, friends, he lets the Lord's name do the talking instead of his own.

The answer is False. Jude says these men “…slander what they do not understand…” So they're loud about things they don't get, friends. Nobody's impressed by a review from someone who never read the book.

The answer is the things they do instinctively. Jude says, “…like irrational animals, they will be destroyed by the things they do instinctively.” They follow their gut, friends, and their gut leads them down. That's the picture he paints.

The answer is profit. Jude says these men “…have rushed for profit into the error of Balaam…” Balaam is the man who was hired to curse Israel (Deut 23:4). Rushed is the word to notice, friends, because they ran toward it.

The answer is True. Jude says these men “…have perished in Korah’s rebellion.” Korah is the one who rose up against Moses (Num 16:1-3). It's the third name in a row, friends, of people who went the wrong direction.

The answer is only themselves. Jude says they're “…shamelessly feasting with you but shepherding only themselves.” A shepherd who looks after one sheep, and it's him. That's not shepherding, friends, that's just grazing.

The answer is fruitless and uprooted. Jude calls them “fruitless trees in autumn, twice dead after being uprooted.” No fruit, and uprooted, friends, that's the picture. It's a rough image, so I'll leave it there.

The answer is blackest darkness. Jude says they're “wandering stars, for whom blackest darkness has been reserved forever.” Stars are supposed to shine, friends, and these ones wander off. The darkness is what's waiting for them. It's heavy, so I'll leave it there.

The answer is the Lord. Enoch prophesied, “Behold, the Lord is coming with myriads of His holy ones…” Enoch is the seventh from Adam, friends, and Jude says he prophesied about these men. The one coming is the Lord.

The answer is False. Enoch says the Lord will “…convict all the ungodly of every ungodly act of wickedness and every harsh word spoken against Him by ungodly sinners.” Both the acts and the harsh words are named, friends. Nothing slips through.

The word is flatter. Jude says they “…flatter others for their own advantage.” It's compliments with a price tag attached, friends. When somebody's being sweet only because they want something, that's this.

The answer is scoffers following their own ungodly desires. Jude quotes the apostles: “In the last times there will be scoffers who will follow after their own ungodly desires.” So the beloved were told ahead of time, friends. When it shows up, it shouldn't catch them off guard.
The answer is False. Jude says, “These are the ones who cause divisions, who are worldly and devoid of the Spirit.” They pull people apart, friends. Bringing believers together isn't what they do.

The answer is True. Jude tells the beloved to “…keep yourselves in the love of God…” He says to do it by building themselves up in their most holy faith and praying in the Holy Spirit. It's something to stay in, friends, like keeping yourself warm in a kitchen with the oven on.

The answer is the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ. Jude says to keep themselves in God's love “…as you await the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ to bring you eternal life.” Waiting here isn't sitting idle, friends, because he's just told them to build up their faith and pray. The mercy comes from Jesus.

The answer is to have mercy on them. Jude says, “And indeed, have mercy on those who doubt…” Doubters get patience, friends. Remember, being unsure about something is not the same as being against it.
The word is fire. Jude says, “…save others by snatching them from the fire…” Snatching is quick and urgent, friends, like pulling a tray out before it burns. It's about getting people out in time.

The answer is unblemished and with great joy. Jude says God is able “…to present you unblemished in His glorious presence, with great joy…” Unblemished, in His glorious presence, with great joy, friends. That's what he says God is able to do.

The answer is True. Jude writes, “…to the only God our Savior be glory, majesty, dominion, and authority through Jesus Christ our Lord before all time, and now, and for all eternity.” Before all time, now, and for all eternity, friends. That's the closing, right there in verse 25.
